J-dore-kurai.reason: Built from kept dore plus gurai; answers need numbers, which are out of scope.

J-docchi-demo.reason: Follows directly from dotchi plus the kept nandemo/dokodemo pattern.

J-kono-hen.reason: koko covers 'around here'; hen would also clash with the kept hen 'weird'.

J-ikutsu.reason: Answers need numbers and counters, which are out of scope; #1556.

J-chan.reason: -san covers name suffixes in speech; -chan is easy to tell from context.

J-kun.reason: Narrower than -chan (boys, juniors); -san always works, and -kun is obvious when heard.

J-ore.reason: Near-synonym of kept watashi; a blunt male register variant with no new meaning.

J-anata.reason: Name plus -san and sotchi ('you') already do the job; anata is better avoided in speech.

J-kare.reason: Names or ano hito do 'he'; the boyfriend sense is topic vocabulary.

J-kanojo.reason: Same as kare: ano hito does 'she', and 'girlfriend' is topic vocabulary.

J-dou-shita.reason: 'dou shita no?' (#285) is the everyday what's-wrong check-in; not obvious from dou + suru.

J-sonna-ni.reason: anmari covers 'not that much'; sonna plus honto? cover the pushback.

J-nan-no.reason: Regular nani + no; nothing new to learn.

J-naze.reason: Formal 'why'; nande / doushite are already kept for conversation.

J-kimi.reason: Used in songs and to juniors; masculine and risky to say. Recognition only.

J-aa-iu.reason: Means the same as kept anna, and is less frequent (#1183).

J-atashi.reason: Casual female variant of watashi; easy to recognise and optional to use.

J-aitsu.reason: Rough, and rude about outsiders. Mostly recognition; ano hito is the safe form.

J-ittai.reason: Emphatic 'on earth'; heard more than said, and not needed to ask anything.

J-otagai.reason: Narrow (#817); mostly in set phrases like otagai-sama.

J-omae.reason: Rough male 'you'; insulting if misused. Recognition only, and drama inflates its count.

J-anta.reason: Blunt 'you'; don't produce it. Recognition only.

J-uchi.reason: The list has no 'home'; uchi ni iru, uchi kuru? and the in-group 'our' are everyday (#113).

J-rei-no.reason: ano already points at shared knowledge (ano mise); rei no is more businesslike.

J-mukou.reason: atchi and asoko cover 'over there' and 'their side' in casual speech.

J-ikurademo.reason: Optional and less frequent (#2178); takusan and ippai handle 'plenty'.

J-aite.reason: hito ('person; others') covers 'the other person' well enough for a learner.

J-docchi-mo.reason: Built from kept dotchi plus mo, like daremo and nanimo; zenbu also covers 'all of them'.

J-mae-ushiro.reason: Spatial mae (eki no mae) is missing because A's mae is time only; ushiro completes the pair.

J-tonari-yoko.reason: Optional; when talking face to face, koko, soko and kotchi already handle locating things.

J-chikaku.reason: Nothing on the list means 'near'; eki no chikaku and chikaku ni are everyday (#464).

J-mawari.reason: minna, hito and hoka no hito cover 'the people around'; it is optional.

J-naka.reason: Same word as the kept naka / soto pair.

J-ue.reason: Same word as the kept ue / shita pair.

J-shita.reason: Same word as the kept ue / shita pair.

J-soto.reason: Same word as the kept naka / soto pair.

J-tonari.reason: Duplicates the tonari / yoko entry, which is also rejected.

J-ushiro.reason: Duplicate; it comes in with the mae / ushiro re-add.

J-koitsu.reason: Rough, like aitsu; recognise it, but kono hito is the safe form.

J-imi.reason: G's 'dou iu imi?' already teaches imi; imi wakannai is built with the kept wakannai.

J-wake.reason: wake da and -wake ja nai are kept; dou iu wake follows from them.
J-wake.coveredBy: F wake da; I -wake ja nai

J-migi-hidari.reason: kotchi, atchi and pointing cover live locating; giving directions is a topic area.

J-sensei.reason: -san covers addressing people; sensei is a role noun, closer to a topic word.

J-kotoba.reason: -tte nani? and nihongo de nante iu? already cover asking about a word.

J-docchi-ka.reason: Follows from dotchi plus the kept nanika/dareka pattern.

J-konna-kanji.reason: The kept 'tte kanji' teaches kanji; donna/konna plus kanji builds it, and dou? also asks it.
